subject: general
question: Which among the following is the largest gland in the human body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The liver** is the** biggest gland in the body **and a digestive system auxiliary organ.
 
• On the right side of the abdomen, it is located.
 
• The falciform ligament divides the liver into two lobes, the left and right.
 
• Hepatocytes, or liver cells, have a unique ability to reproduce in response to any type of liver injury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Perspiration glands** are little tubular structures that create sweat on the surface of the skin. **Sweat glands **are an example of an exocrine gland, which produces and secretes chemicals onto an epithelial surface via a duct.
 
• **The mammary gland **is made up of connective tissue, fat, and tissue, and it houses milk-producing glands. 
 
• **Esophageal cardiac glands **are mucous glands in the lamina propria mucosae that are placed near the cardiac orifice (esophago-gastric junction).
